newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says China Eastern talk premature.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says China Eastern talk premature.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Monday it was premature to discuss whether the Hong Kong flag carrier was interested in taking a stake in or forming a business alliance with China Eastern Airlines (CEA).

"Our present line is that it's far too early to say we are interested since we have not yet made any contact with China Eastern," Kwan Chuk-fai, Cathay Pacific's manager of corporate communications, told Reuters.
Kwan was quoted by the Hong Kong Economic Journal as saying Cathay was interested in considering taking a stake in or forming a business alliance with CEA.
CEA is seeking a dual listing in Hong Kong and New York and is expected to launch its initial public offering in January or early February.
CEA's annual report for 1995 said it posted unaudited net profit of 500 million yuan (US$60.2 million) on turnover of seven billion yuan. It gave no comparative figures.
The airline has a fleet of 39 McDonnell Douglas, Airbus and Fokker planes flying 88 domestic and 23 foreign routes.
